topicName: Artifact Registry: Container Image and Package Management
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Artifact Registry: Container Image and Package Management on Google Cloud"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Artifact Registry is a fully managed, scalable, and secure service for storing, managing, and securing your container images and language packages. It acts as a single source of truth for your artifacts, integrating seamlessly with Google Cloud services like Cloud Build, Cloud Run, and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Benefits of Using Artifact Registry"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Centralized Artifact Storage: Provides a single location to store all your container images and packages, simplifying management and version control."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhanced Security: Offers fine-grained access control, vulnerability scanning, and integration with Google Cloud's security features to protect your artifacts."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved Collaboration: Enables teams to easily share and collaborate on artifacts, promoting consistency and efficiency."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Streamlined Deployment: Integrates seamlessly with Google Cloud deployment services, making it easy to deploy your applications."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Support for Multiple Formats: Supports various package formats, including Docker images, Helm charts, Maven, npm, Python packages, and more."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting Up Artifact Registry"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you begin, ensure you have a Google Cloud project and the Artifact Registry API enabled. You can enable the API through the Google Cloud Console or using the gcloud CLI."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"gcloud services enable artifactregistry.googleapis.com"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Repository"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"A repository is a named storage location for your artifacts. You need to create a repository before you can push or pull images and packages. Choose a repository format that matches the type of artifact you want to store (e.g., 'docker' for container images, 'npm' for Node.js packages)."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"gcloud artifacts repositories create my-repo \\\n    --repository-format=docker \\\n    --location=us-central1 \\\n    --description=\"My Docker image repository\""},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'my-repo' with your desired repository name and 'us-central1' with your preferred Google Cloud region. The '--repository-format' flag specifies the type of artifacts the repository will store."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Pushing a Container Image"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To push a container image to Artifact Registry, you first need to tag the image with the Artifact Registry repository URL. The URL format is 'us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[PROJECT-ID]/[REPOSITORY]/[IMAGE]:[TAG]'."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"docker tag my-image:latest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/my-image:latest"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'my-image:latest' with your local image name and tag, 'my-project' with your Google Cloud project ID, and 'my-repo' with the name of your Artifact Registry repository."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Authenticate Docker to Artifact Registry. This step is crucial for pushing and pulling images."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Finally, push the tagged image to Artifact Registry."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/my-image:latest"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Pulling a Container Image"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"To pull a container image from Artifact Registry, use the 'docker pull' command with the Artifact Registry repository URL."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"docker pull us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/my-image:latest"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Managing Packages (Example: npm)"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Artifact Registry also supports managing language packages. Here's an example of how to publish and install npm packages."},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, configure npm to use your Artifact Registry repository. Create a '.npmrc' file in your project directory with the following content:"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"//us-central1-npm.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/:_authToken=\"$(gcloud auth print-access-token)\"\n@my-project:registry=https://us-central1-npm.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'my-project' and 'my-repo' with your Google Cloud project ID and Artifact Registry repository name, respectively."},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Publish your npm package:"},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"npm publish"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install the npm package:"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"npm install @my-project/my-package"},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Access Control"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Artifact Registry uses Identity and Access Management (IAM) to control access to your repositories. You can grant users or service accounts permissions to push, pull, or manage artifacts. Common roles include 'roles/artifactregistry.reader', 'roles/artifactregistry.writer', and 'roles/artifactregistry.admin'."},{"order":38,"type":"code","text":"gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding my-project \\\n    --member=\"user:john.doe@example.com\" \\\n    --role=\"roles/artifactregistry.reader\""},{"order":39,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"Artifact Registry provides a robust and secure solution for managing your container images and language packages on Google Cloud. By centralizing your artifacts and integrating with other Google Cloud services, it simplifies deployment, enhances security, and improves collaboration within your development teams."}]
